knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=2 x + 4 y + 4 z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨3 u^{2},\,u - v^{2},\,v^{2}⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:v\geq0\}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

*Hint: You may use $\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=2 v \sqrt{72 u^{2} + 1}$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The area factor is supplied. Substitute each coordinate into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 \left(3 u^{2}\right) + 4 \left(u - v^{2}\right) + 4 \left(v^{2}\right)\\&=6 u^{2} + 4 u.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor:

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D 2 v \sqrt{72 u^{2} + 1} \left(6 u^{2} + 4 u\right)\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The missing expression is $2 v \sqrt{72 u^{2} + 1} \left(6 u^{2} + 4 u\right)$. The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=- 2 x + 2 z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u v,\,u^{2},\,v^{2}⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

*Hint: You may use $\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{4 u^{4} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}}$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The area factor is supplied. Substitute each coordinate into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- 2 \left(u v\right) + 2 \left(v^{2}\right)\\&=- 2 u v + 2 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor. The missing expression is

$$
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u v + 2 v^{2}\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{4 u^{4} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u v + 2 v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{4 u^{4} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u v + 2 v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \left(4 u^{4} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}\right)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u v + 2 v^{2}\right)\\&\quad\cdot \left(4 u^{4} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}\right)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u v + 2 v^{2}\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{4 u^{4} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}}\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=x y + 2 z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u^{2},\,2 v⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

*Hint: You may use $\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{16 u^{2} + 4}$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The area factor is supplied. Substitute each coordinate into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=\left(u\right) \left(u^{2}\right) + 2 \left(2 v\right)\\&=u^{3} + 4 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor:

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D \sqrt{16 u^{2} + 4} \left(u^{3} + 4 v\right)\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The missing expression is $\sqrt{16 u^{2} + 4} \left(u^{3} + 4 v\right)$. The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.
